notes: 300 hours of daily-activity motion across 1,200 sequences from 264 participants at 50 indoor/outdoor locations covering 20 scenarios (~15 min/recording, 400 km travelled); 230 h carry natural-language motion narration (310.5K sentences). Hardware-synchronised multimodal rig: Project Aria smart glasses (2 IMUs at 800 Hz and 1 kHz plus magnetometer/barometer, video, eye tracking, SLAM cameras), two 'miniAria' wristbands, and an Xsens MVN Link suit with 17 body-worn inertial trackers at 240 Hz providing metric 3D world-frame ground truth. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0 (confirmed on the GitHub release page: 'Data and code may not be used for commercial purposes'; per-sub-dataset licenses are bundled in the repo). Access requires accepting the licence and emailing a request via projectaria.com to receive a URL-JSON file, then downloading with the official `nymeriaplus-download` CLI from github.com/facebookresearch/nymeria_dataset (parallelizable with -n, filterable with -s). Downloads are organized per (sequence, group); the IMU-relevant groups are `body_raw` (Xsens: body/xdata.mvnx, xdata.npz, xdata.healthcheck) and `timesync_and_imu` (per-recording motion.vrs for head/lwrist/rwrist/observer). The GitHub page states the full corpus is ~80 TB across ~1,100 sequences if every download group is taken; downloading only body/IMU groups is far smaller. A 2026 successor, NymeriaPlus (arXiv:2603.18496, 6 pages), extends the release with optimized MHR/SMPL motion formats, 3D/2D object bounding boxes, and 3D object reconstruction over the same capture sessions; local review copy saved as nymeriaplus_paper.pdf alongside the primary Nymeria paper.pdf. Verified 2026-09-09.
